title: Quasi-compactness of an algebraic stack detected by a surjection
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], with quasi-compactness as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Then $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact if and only if there exist a quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal V$ over $S$ and a surjective morphism $\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$. Surjective means that every object of $\mathcal X$ over a field becomes isomorphic to the image of an object of $\mathcal V$ after a field extension. Equivalently, $\mathcal X$ has a smooth surjective scheme atlas whose source is affine, or whose source is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No representability, smoothness, quasi-compactness or finite-type assumption is imposed on the morphism $\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$, and neither stack is assumed Deligne--Mumford. The empty stack is allowed.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), equivalence of (2), (3) and (5); Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective) for field-extension-local surjectivity.

proof.text: Assume there is a surjection $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$ with $\mathcal V$ quasi-compact. By [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] choose a smooth surjective atlas $a:U\to\mathcal V$ with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], $|a|$ is surjective, $|f|$ is continuous, and the topology on $|U|$ is its scheme topology. The stated field-extension lifting condition on $f$ makes $|f|$ surjective: every representative of a target point lifts after extension, which does not change its point class. Given an open cover $(O_i)$ of $|\mathcal X|$, the sets $|a|^{-1}(|f|^{-1}(O_i))$ form an open cover of $|U|$. By [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] finitely many cover $|U|$. Since $|f|\circ|a|$ is surjective, the corresponding $O_i$ cover $|\mathcal X|$. Thus $|\mathcal X|$ is quasi-compact. This argument uses no representability of $f$.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), proof of (5) implies (1) and (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:T\to\mathcal X$ by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and an affine open cover $(j_i:T_i\hookrightarrow T)$ by [lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover]. By [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image], each $q_i=pj_i$ is representable and smooth. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] it is flat and locally of finite presentation. Regard $T_i$ as an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Then [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open] says that $W_i=|q_i|(|T_i|)$ is open in $|\mathcal X|$. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], $|p|$ is surjective; the affine opens cover $T$, so the $W_i$ cover $|\mathcal X|$. None of these statements restricts $\mathcal X$ to a Deligne--Mumford stack.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), proof of (5) implies (1) and (1) implies (2).

proof.text: The quasi-compactness of $|\mathcal X|$ proved in step 1 selects a finite set $J$ with $\bigcup_{j\in J}W_j=|\mathcal X|$. Form the scheme $A=\coprod_{j\in J}T_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its coprojections are disjoint open immersions covering $A$. Write $T_j\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $A\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{j\in J}R_j)$, so $A$ is affine. Its structural map to $S$ is induced by the structural maps of the $T_j$. This includes $J=\varnothing$: the product is the zero ring and $A$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), last three sentences; schemes.tex Tag 01I5 (lemma-disjoint-union-affines).

proof.text: The morphisms $q_j:T_j\to\mathcal X$ give objects on the disjoint open cover of $A$ from step 3. Its inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. On distinct components their overlap is empty, so the overlap isomorphisms and cocycle condition are unique; on each component use the identity. Etale stack descent in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] glues these objects to a morphism $q:A\to\mathcal X$ restricting to each $q_j$. This also applies to the empty cover. Regard $A$ as an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; the representable diagonal of $\mathcal X$ makes $q$ representable by [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability]. Each restriction is smooth by step 2, so source locality in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] makes $q$ smooth. Its point image contains every $W_j$ and hence all of $|\mathcal X|$. Since $q$ is representable, [lem-sfb-representable-stack-point-surjectivity] makes it surjective after every scheme base change. Thus $q$ is the required affine smooth surjective atlas.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), construction of the finite disjoint-union atlas; Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective) only for the representable map q.

proof.text: An affine atlas source is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so the affine-atlas condition implies the quasi-compact-atlas condition. By [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] the latter is exactly quasi-compactness of $\mathcal X$. Conversely this definition already supplies such a quasi-compact atlas. A quasi-compact $\mathcal X$ supplies a surjection from a quasi-compact algebraic stack by taking $\mathcal V=\mathcal X$ and $f=\mathrm{id}$: a field-valued object lifts to itself without extension. Together with steps 1--4 this proves every equivalence. The empty stack is included: its identity and the empty affine atlas satisfy all conditions, and all point-cover arguments above allow an empty finite subcover.
